prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_G:
Summary (≤500 words; policy-focused, non-ideological)

Core objective and process
- Withdraw from the European Union by repealing the European Communities Act, ending budget contributions, restoring UK legal primacy, and regaining an independent seat at bodies like the WTO.
- Two-year transition managed by a cabinet committee to review, repeal, or replace EU-derived laws and to create UK policies for agriculture, fisheries, trade, and other areas.

Economy and regulation
- Maintain tariff-free/bilateral trade with European neighbors, pursue broader global trade links (Commonwealth, North America, Asia), and cooperate on shared issues (environment, residence rights).
- Systematic deregulation with a presumption to scrap rules unless clearly necessary, prioritizing relief for small businesses; remove measures such as the Working Time Directive.
- Use the claimed c. £1bn/year saved from EU contributions to raise the state pension by £2/week; temporarily increase borrowing by £3bn/year for immediate tax cuts and targeted spending, notably on defense.
- Immediate tax changes: halve council tax for all households; abolish the 10% income tax band; reinstate dividend tax credits for pension funds; raise the inheritance tax threshold to £500,000.
- Longer term: simplify and lower taxes, replace VAT with a wholesale sales tax, merge National Insurance with income tax, and consider a flat tax.

Health, welfare, and pensions
- Decentralize NHS management; cap bureaucracy; restore a single accountable clinical manager (“matron”) model; scrap Strategic Health Authorities; reopen GP surgeries evenings/weekends; ease target-driven constraints on clinicians; consider complementary private insurance; remove EU limits on supplements/herbals and the Working Time Directive in health.
- Simplify and reduce means-testing in benefits; prioritize transparency and work incentives; avoid large-scale “active labour market” programs without proven outcomes.
- Pensions: raise state pensions by £2/week (via EU savings); reinstate pension fund tax credits (~£5bn/year); restore full uprating for expatriate pensioners; acknowledge need for higher saving/longer working over time.

Education
- Grant greater school autonomy; scrap SATs; empower heads to exclude; provide specialist provision for excluded pupils; allow limited selection and specialisms; emphasize sport, trips, and core standards; remove central interference in exam standards.
- Expand access to independent schooling via assisted places, vouchers, or tax reliefs.
- Universities: review and defund low-standard courses; fully fund high-standard courses; cancel top-up fees; provide maintenance grants; scrap student loans; charge EU students full overseas rates; expand technical colleges.

Law and order and immigration
- Increase local accountability of police; reduce paperwork; strengthen magistrates; review sentencing with clear minima and maxima; build prisons as needed; protect homeowners defending property.
- Target near zero net immigration: introduce a points-based system; equal treatment for EU and non-EU applicants; tighter family reunification; reinstate embarkation controls; language/civics tests; health checks; redefine and strictly apply refugee criteria (no claims via safe third countries); accelerate removals.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Replace CAP with guaranteed minimum prices/deficiency payments; reduce bureaucracy; improve biosecurity; reopen small abattoirs; support local food, green/hill farming, young farmers; consider restoring the Milk Marketing Board.
- Exit the CFP; reassert control over UK waters; strengthen enforcement; regulate gear/mesh; use fallow zones for stock recovery.

Defense and foreign affairs
- Maintain NATO alignment; disengage from EU defense structures; retain independent international representation; reverse force cuts; increase defense spending; prioritize domestic procurement; deploy only for clear national interest.

Energy, environment, and transport
- Halt wind turbine rollout; build new nuclear fission plants; invest in fusion R&D; develop clean-coal technologies.
- Set environmental policy domestically; prioritize recycling, habitat protection, green farming; restrict GM crop planting until long-term safety is proven.
- Continue rail upgrades; consider reintegrating track and train management; resist EU transport directives; increase road investment; localize traffic management; raise some speed limits where safe; limit speed cameras to proven danger sites.

Governance
- Preserve existing national institutions; oppose further dilution of the revising chamber’s independence.
- Citizen-initiated referendums: if 5% of the electorate signs within six months, a binding national referendum is held.
- Consider “English-only” legislative days at Westminster; abolish English regional assemblies and related quangos.
- Redirect business rates and some duties to local councils; increase local autonomy and transparency; reduce politically driven posts; promote recycling.
- Repeal the Human Rights Act; maintain ECHR principles; drop ID cards; repeal the Hunting Act.

TEXT_C:
This 2005 manifesto proposes changes across the economy, environment, welfare, public services, transport, democracy, and international policy.

Economy and taxation
- More progressive income tax bands (illustrative: 50% over £50k; 60% over £100k) and additional corporation tax bands (up to 40% on profits over £1.5m).
- Shift taxation from labour and consumption to resource use and pollution: abolish National Insurance, phase out VAT, introduce revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes (including aviation fuel; levies on plastic bags).
- Pilot a Land Value Tax set locally to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Promote economic localisation: community banks, credit unions, local currencies, support for small businesses; oppose joining the euro; seek reform of global trade rules.
- Job creation via renewable energy, low‑carbon transport, and zero‑waste industries; defend workplace rights and reduce working hours.
- Supplement GDP with well‑being metrics (e.g., ISEW/MDP).

Energy and climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: cut CO2 by 20% (2010), 50% (2020), 85% (2030); develop full carbon trading.
- Replace domestic energy VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax based on fuel carbon content; abolish standing charges; protect low‑use consumers.
- Reach 40% renewable energy by 2020; redirect nuclear subsidies to renewables; deploy solar, small‑scale wind, offshore wind/wave, and biogas.
- Warmer Homes Act to cut domestic energy demand 30% in 10 years; local “Smart Energy Councils” targeting 45% emissions cuts by 2020.
- Decommission nuclear plants at end of life; end nuclear R&D support.

Welfare, housing, work and families
- Phase in a universal, non‑means‑tested Citizen’s Income; retain specialist benefits and initially retain housing benefit.
- Introduce a universal Citizen’s Pension, earnings‑linked, replacing Pension Credit.
- Simplify child support and increase child benefit in the first phase; end the Working Time Directive opt‑out; explore a 35‑hour week; expand early‑years centres.
- Boost affordable housing: let councils reinvest sale receipts, support self‑build co‑ops, apply LVT, and upgrade insulation/efficiency.

Health and education
- Restore a universal NHS free at point of use; end PPPs and resist service liberalisation.
- Abolish prescription charges; reintroduce free eye tests and NHS dental care; expand access to complementary treatments.
- Increase health funding to about 9% of GNP; consider a hypothecated NHS tax; redirect future defence savings to health.
- Increase education funding (pre‑school and post‑16), scrap tuition fees, restore maintenance grants, abolish SATs, and promote individual learning plans.

Transport
- Target a 10% road‑traffic reduction by 2010; divert £30bn from road building to public transport; re‑regulate buses.
- Return rail and Tube to public ownership; expand lines, stations, freight, and light rail.
- Reflect full motoring costs via congestion charging/road pricing; raise fuel duty; abolish car tax discs; vary freight duty by size/axle/pollution; fund R&D in efficient vehicles.
- Restrain aviation growth: oppose new runways, ban night flights, seek EU aviation fuel tax; tax domestic flight emissions; raise Air Passenger Duty; shift short‑haul to rail.

Environment, food, and animal welfare
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration, reduce packaging, set recycled content standards, create a Zero Waste Agency; aim for 60% domestic recycling by 2010.
- Environmental Protection Commission; eco‑taxes on aggregates, pesticides, organochlorines, fossil fuels; strengthen chemicals regulation.
- Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation, and nanotechnology; oppose patents on natural resources.
- Animal welfare: extend hunting bans, replace vivisection, end live exports, ban battery eggs (including enriched), tighten broiler rules, ban fur imports.
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; support local food chains; ban GM food.
- Replace CAP/CFP with policies backing local markets, biodiversity, and sustainable incomes for farming and fishing.

Crime and justice
- Prevention through urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, more caretakers; treat drug use as a health issue; reject ID cards and redirect funds to prevention.
- Strengthen community policing, accountability, and local stations; revive community wardens/keepers.
- Tighten gun laws: quantitative lethality threshold, broader prohibitions, treat deactivated guns as active for licensing, single rigorous licensing, ongoing expert review.
- Expand restorative justice; enhance responses to hate crimes, violence against women; support stronger disability rights.

Democracy and constitutional reform
- Oppose national ID cards.
- Devolve power to local and regional levels; introduce proportional representation for local and national elections.
- Enable local recall (40%) and referenda (20% trigger); empower local taxation via LVT.
- Fully elected upper chamber by PR; draft a written constitution; disestablish the state church; limit monarchy’s formal roles.
- Oppose the proposed EU constitution while advocating EU reform to enhance democracy and sustainability.

International policy
- Ethical foreign policy: prioritise diplomacy, UN peacekeeping, and conflict prevention; withdraw troops from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers.
- Reduce defence spending to EU average; decommission nuclear weapons; end arms export subsidies/credits; negotiate an Arms Trade Treaty; ban use of depleted uranium.
- Raise aid to at least 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest countries; support a Tobin tax; enable North–South carbon finance flows.
- Reform UN Security Council (end permanent seats; majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank.
- Overhaul global trade rules to permit localisation and sustainability, replacing or modifying WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade.
- Asylum/migration: uphold refugee rights, speed decisions, allow work/benefits, provide independent appeals; ratify the UN Migrant Workers Convention; review domestic asylum law; support improved EU standards.

Judge whether TEXT_G or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_G" | "TEXT_C"
}
